title: Granular length adaptivity and quantized kernel profiles (working draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note explores a fine-grained approach for handling dynamic sequence length distributions in the serving runtime. The goal is to reduce wasted compute from coarse padding while retaining kernel stability and predictable latency. We combine: (1) granular length adaptivity (small, data-driven length groups), (2) profiled/quantized kernel profiles that trade throughput vs memory for each length group, and (3) KV cache-aware partial-shard serving to reduce re-computation on cache hits.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Modern workloads exhibit heavy-tailed sequence length distributions: a large fraction of requests are short but a meaningful tail is long. Coarse bucketing (e.g., 8/16/32/64) wastes tokens for the common short requests; overly fine bucketing increases scheduling overhead and kernel variants.
- Kernel performance often depends strongly on shape and quantization strategy: int8 kernels may be fastest for mid-length requests but have memory/accuracy tradeoffs for long sequences.
- KV cache introduces fragmentation: prefix-cached sessions can mean trailing generation lengths vary per-request and can break batching assumptions.

Design goals and constraints:
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= configured SLO per plan (e.g., 150ms for hosted tier), preserve p99 guardrails.
- Throughput / cost: reduce effective tokens-served by lowering average padding, maintain GPU utilization >= 60% in steady state.
- Operational complexity: limit number of kernel variants per model to a manageable set (<= 6 default profiles).
- Safety: deterministic fallbacks to a conservative profile when profile selection fails.

Key concepts introduced in this doc:
1) Granular groups (GG): small, contiguous length ranges derived from incoming length histograms. Unlike fixed power-of-two bucket boundaries we compute adaptive boundaries such that short-request bins are finer (e.g., 1-8,9-16,17-24) and tail bins grow wider.

2) Kernel profiles (KP): each KP is a pair of (kernel variant, quantization profile, max-gemm-shape-hint, microbatch-config). For a given GG we maintain a ranked list of KPs ordered by expected cost-latency tradeoff.

3) Profile selector (PS): runtime component that maps an incoming request (current_prefix_len + expected_remaining_tokens and SLO class) to a GG and picks an optimal KP. Selection can be immediate (heuristic) or learned via small in-prod experiments.

4) KV-fragment stitcher: when a request partially hits the KV cache (prefix cached), we use prefix-length aware grouping to allow the remainder to be batched with compatible requests, and avoid re-encoding cached segments.

Adaptive grouping algorithm (high level):
- Maintain a sliding-window histogram H of request "effective sequence length" (prefix_len + expected_tokens). Window default: 10k requests or 5 minutes.
- Compute candidate boundaries by minimizing expected padding waste per group subject to: min_bin_width=4 tokens for bins <=32, growth_factor<=1.5 for successive bins, max_bins=18.
- Prioritize creating denser bins in the 0-64 token region; allow coarser bins beyond 512 tokens.
- Recompute boundaries when real reduction in padding waste >2% or at low-traffic safe intervals.

Pseudo code (selection):
- input: prefix_len, expected_remaining, slo_class
- effective_len = prefix_len + expected_remaining
- gg = find_group_for_length(effective_len)
- candidate_kps = profile_catalog[model][gg]
- for kp in candidate_kps ordered by rank:
    if kp.available_on_device(request.device) and kp.latency_estimate(effective_len, slo_class) <= slo_budget:
        return kp
- return conservative_kp

Kernel profile catalog and profiling strategy:
- For each model, build KP catalog offline using a matrix sweep: lengths in {8,16,32,64,128,256,512}, quant levels {fp16, int8-dq, int8-perchannel}, and kernels {fused-attn-v1, split-ffn, tiled-gemm}. Capture: per-token latency, peak-scratch-mem, accuracy delta vs baseline FP16 (for int8 variants), and effective tradeoff score = latency_adjusted + alpha * mem_penalty + beta * accuracy_penalty.
- KP archetypes: "low-latency (short)" tuned for <64 tokens, "balanced" tuned for 64-256, "high-capacity" tuned for >256. Each archetype maps to different quantization.

KV cache integration notes:
- Cacheable prefix detection: identify when a request has a full prefix hit vs partial. In partial-hit case, the remaining generation often has lower variance and can be bucketed more tightly.
- Partial-shard batching: allow a batch to be composed of requests with identical suffix-length expectations and identical cache boundary offset modulo a small delta (e.g., <=4 tokens). The scheduler should prioritize forming those micro-batches to utilize fast KP variants.
- Cache stitcher must validate KV compatibility across different kernel variants. If the selected KP uses a different attention kernel that expects a different KV memory layout, the stitcher should either transpose/convert KV (expensive) or fall back to a compatible KP. We prefer cataloging compatible KP pairings ahead of time to avoid runtime conversions.

Progressive padding and graceful degradation:
- For extremely latency-sensitive requests we allow progressive padding: start with small padding to get early partial tokens streaming and then later re-pack the remainder if more tokens arrive (optimizes for tail-token latency).
- Fallbacks: if profile selection cannot find an available KP within latency budget, divert to "preemptive-evict" policy that reduces batch size and uses the conservative KP to preserve p99. Track metrics for all fallbacks.

Operational rollout plan:
1) Offline profiling job: generate KP catalog for top-10 models by traffic. (JIRA-RI-842).
2) Canary: enable PS for a small fraction (1%) of traffic with telemetry capturing per-request selected KP, predicted vs observed latency, padding waste, and accuracy deltas.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% and 100% with automated rollback triggers: increase in p99 by >10% or token cost >8%.

Metrics to capture (must be exported to Console dashboards):
- padding_waste_percent (by GG)
- kp_selection_rate (per KP)
- kp_miss_fallback_rate
- p50/p95/p99 latency by KP and GG
- tokens_served_per_request (effective)
- kv_partial_hit_rate and stitch_fallback_rate

Experiments and early results (toy runs):
- Simulated on synthetic distribution (70%<=16 tokens, 20% 17-64, 10% >64): granular groups reduced avg padding tokens by 38% vs power-of-two bucketing; approximate cost saving 24% after accounting for slight drop in GPU efficiency.
- Int8-dq KP for short bins showed 1.6x throughput improvements at ~0.4% accuracy hit on top-1 logits on an eval set.

Open questions and risk areas:
- How fast can we safely change GG boundaries in-prod without causing oscillations or thrash on the scheduler? (Investigate hysteresis and minimum time between changes.)
- Compatibility explosion: cataloging KP pairwise compatibilities for many models and HW targets may blow up. Need heuristics to prune unlikely pairings.
- Observability: tracing selection -> kernel invocation -> actual kernel path executed is crucial; currently some low-level kernels do not emit enough telemetry.
- Accuracy monitoring for quantized KPs: need automatic eval hooks to detect drift.

Backward compatibility and fallbacks:
- Default behavior when feature disabled: single conservative KP (current baseline). Switch is opt-in per deployment and per-model.
- Config knobs: per-model max_kps, enable_partial_shard_batching, gg_recompute_interval, min_bin_width.

Next steps / action items:
- (Asha) land profiling harness to produce KP catalog artifacts for the 3 highest-traffic models (due 2024-09-10).
- (Marcus) prototype PS heuristics in the scheduler and wire lightweight telemetry (due 2024-09-17).
- (Sofia) work with SRE to create canary plan and rollback rules (due 2024-09-12).
- (Diego) audit current kernel telemetry and add selection -> kernel mapping traces (due 2024-09-20).

Appendix: short example trace for partial KV-hit case:
- request A: prefix_len=48 (cached), expected_remaining=32 -> effective_len=80 -> GG=64-96 -> selected KP=balanced-int8
- request B: prefix_len=0, expected_remaining=80 -> effective_len=80 -> same GG -> selected KP=balanced-int8
- scheduler groups A and B into same micro-batch, B computes full KV; A uses cached KV pointers. KP compatibility check passes (both use same attention kernel layout) so no KV conversion required.

Concluding note:
This draft attempts to balance practical operational constraints (limited KP variants, deterministic fallbacks) with improved cost/latency tradeoffs via data-driven grouping and quantized kernels. The remaining work is implementation (catalog generation, PS integration), canarying and adding robust telemetry for production observability. Feedback welcome — especially on the GG recompute heuristics and safe rollback thresholds.
